messages:
Elena Gomez: Thanks for joining the all-hands Q&A thread. A few folks asked about benefits, comp band timing, and how global hires are handled. I'll collect the questions here and get concrete answers. Short and practical please.

Kwaku Mensah: Two quick things from Eng managers: 1) for global hires in EMEA/APAC, do we use the US band midpoint or a local band? 2) equity refresh cadence question — is that annual or on a case-by-case?

Priya Patel: Good ones. TL;DR: we operate a regional pay framework — we map to local market bands for base pay, then adjust equity targets by role-level and region. Refreshes are generally annual but can be earlier for retention cases with director+ sign-off. More details below.

Lina Chen: For international folks who relocate to the US mid-cycle, do they move to US comp immediately or at next review? Also how does PTO/prorated benefits transfer?

Priya Patel: If someone relocates and their legal employment moves to the US entity, we trigger a comp re-eval within 30 days; any increases are applied pro-rata and aligned with payroll cutoffs. PTO accruals are preserved where legally possible; benefits enrollment windows apply, so managers should coordinate with people ops and HRBP.

Marco Alvarez: Finance note: payroll cutoffs + entity transfers need ~2 weeks lead time. For payroll timing questions, always flag on the form so we can queue it.

Kwaku Mensah: Got it. Next: appeals/feedback after calibration. What's the formal window and what evidence do we accept? We had someone ask if peer surveys can be submitted post-calibration.

Priya Patel: Appeals window = 14 calendar days from the calibration outcome notification. We accept new, verifiable evidence (peer quotes, product metrics, logs) that wasn't available during calibration. We don't re-run full calibrations for marginal noise; appeals go to a small panel (manager+director+people ops) and are for clear misses.

Lina Chen: On promotion evidence: can mentoring/mentee outcomes be part of the case? We have a lot of informal mentors.

Elena Gomez: Absolutely — mentoring that leads to measurable outcomes (e.g., mentee promoted, project led by mentee, org-wide process adoption) is strong evidence. If it's informal, ask mentees for a 1-2 line note to include.

peopleops-bot: :loudspeaker: Quick links: handbook: https://intranet.redwood/handbook/promo-and-comp; appeal form: /forms/comp-appeal; relocation guide: /hr/relocation.

Kwaku Mensah: Parental leave and top-ups 1: are managers supposed to request top-ups for ICs who are returning part-time? What's the policy on bonus proration during leave?

Priya Patel: Parents: base parental leave is 16 weeks full-pay for primary caregivers, 8 weeks for secondary (US policy). Top-ups for statutory differences in other countries are handled case-by-case. Bonus proration: bonus payouts are pro-rated based on time worked during the performance period unless there's an explicit manager recommendation and approval from finance+people ops.

Lina Chen: Would love an example scenario for bonus proration in the handbook (numbers). Helps managers explain to folks.

Elena Gomez: Good suggestion  I'll add a simple example to the FAQ doc today.

Kwaku Mensah: One more practical item: manager calibration training. Can we request a 1-hour refresher before the next cycle?

Priya Patel: Yes. We're running two live calibration workshops: 2024-08-01 10:00 PT and 2024-08-08 16:00 PT. Sign-up sheet: https://calendar.redwood/cals/promo-workshops. We also have the recorded microtraining on the hub.

allhands-bot: :white_check_mark: Reminder: promotion packets due 2024-08-12 23:59 PT. Managers, submit via /forms/promo-packet.

Marco Alvarez: For equity vesting questions: cliff remains 1 year, standard schedule 4 years with monthly thereafter. For newly hired folks we can offer accelerated partial vesting only via exec approval in rare retention cases.

Lina Chen: Transparency ask: will we publish band midpoints and ranges publicly in the handbook? Some teams want more clarity.

Elena Gomez: We're publishing band ranges (low-mid-high) for most IC levels next week. Compensation committee reviewed privacy and legal implications; ranges will be shown at a regional granularity, not individual offers. We'll share a write-up on how to interpret them.

Kwaku Mensah: Thanks 1 super helpful. If any manager wants to DM examples or edge cases (international hires, equity swaps on transfers), tag @Priya or @Elena and we'll triage.

Priya Patel: I'll consolidate this thread into an FAQ doc and post in #people-ops by EOD tomorrow. If there are specific edge-case items, please DM. :sparkles:
